result.title: From Evaluation to Evolution: Benchmarking Image Editing and Evolving Image Models
result.summary: Real-world image editing requires coordinating multiple visual transformations with content preservation and reference constraints, yet aggregate scores can readily obscure unmet local requirements. Effective evaluation must therefore identify local failures and translate them into priorities for subsequent model improvement. We introduce WeGenEditBench, comprising 2,740 evaluation instances and 148 task types across single-image, text-intensive, and multi-reference editing. Pre-generated checklists shared across models decompose each request into atomic requirements; item-level deductions and visual evidence are established first and then summarized into scores for edit execution, preservation, visual quality, and task-specific correctness. To support the experience-acquisition component of recursive self-improvement (RSI), we develop WeGenEvoStudio, a unified multi-agent harness for RSI-oriented learning that integrates model-conditioned failure diagnosis, retrieval-grounded data construction, supervised adaptation, and re-evaluation. Among 15 evaluated configurations, GPT-Image-2 leads single-image editing with an Overall score of 4.076, while Seedream-5.0-Pro leads text-intensive editing at 4.291. Evolution experiments across four generation and editing benchmarks demonstrate substantial targeted gains: on their report-selected Top-5 single-image targets, FLUX.2 [dev] improves Overall from 1.083 to 3.517, while Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 gains 13.2%. Together, our benchmark and harness provide a foundation for developing more reliable image models through interpretable evaluation and feedback-driven learning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出图像编辑基准 WeGenEditBench，用预生成清单将请求拆成原子要求并逐项扣分、附视觉证据，同时构建 WeGenEvoStudio 多智能体流程做失败诊断、数据构造、监督适配与再评估，验证针对性迭代带来的提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽聚焦图像编辑而非 LVR 内部状态，其原子要求清单、逐项视觉证据和失败驱动再训练，可能为诊断视觉推理中「哪条证据或要求未被满足」及监督分配提供评价设计参考，需核查可迁移性。
